decisions.headline: A control is referenced in run state by its bare id (`insight`), not its full `id@version` ref (`insight@1`).
decisions.problem: Writing "the failures as input" into `steps.<node>.controls` needs a key a Step's own `in:` expression can actually address — but the expression grammar's path syntax (S8: `path := ident ("." ident | "[" integer "]")*`) has no room for `@` inside an ident, so a dict keyed by the full versioned ref (`insight@1`) would be structurally unreachable from any `in:` mapping.
options_rejected: Key by the full ref anyway, accepting that S2.2's reserved path is only reachable by other means (e.g. tooling reading the record directly, never a Step's own expression): rejected — this would make the very field S10.2 asks a repair to read from useless to the one place S10.2 says it should be read from.

Invent a sanitised key (e.g. replacing `@`/`.` with `_`): rejected — a fabricated encoding scheme not grounded in anything the spec or the expression grammar already defines, and harder to predict for a process author writing an `in:` mapping by hand.
decisions.cost_to_change: Localized to _step_record_from's one dict comprehension; no change to the durable record itself, which still stores the full versioned ref for audit purposes.

evidence.claim: The expression tokenizer's ident pattern (definition/expressions.py's _TOKEN_RE) has no `@` in its character class; parsing a path segment containing `@` fails.
evidence.source: src/sulis_workflows/definition/expressions.py, read directly this session and in earlier WP-01 work this session's context carries forward.

evidence.claim: A run resolves exactly one version of each reference once, at run start (spec S1.2: "Resolution happens once, when a run starts") — so within one run, a control's bare id and its resolved version are in 1:1 correspondence, and the bare id alone is unambiguous.

decisions.revisit_if: A future work package lets one Step reference two different controls that happen to share a bare id but differ only in version within the same run — not possible under the current registry/resolution model, so not expected.

lessons.maxim: When wiring a new runtime data path into a place an author-facing expression is meant to read it, check the expression grammar's own lexical rules before choosing the key shape — a dict key that looks natural in Python (a full `id@version` ref) can be structurally unreachable from the DSL that is actually supposed to consume it.
lessons.incident: The first draft of _step_record_from keyed steps.<node>.controls by the control's full ref (e.g. "insight@1"); this would have compiled and run without error but made the field unreachable from any real `in:` mapping, since the expression tokenizer's ident pattern excludes `@` — caught before shipping only because a test was written that actually exercises an `in:` mapping reading the new field, not one that only checked the record's own shape in isolation.
lessons.destination: Any future work in this repository that adds a new run-state path meant to be read by a Step's own `in:`/`if:`/expression field — write the test as an actual expression reading that path, not just an assertion on the stored data structure.
